stem: A 26-year-old man comes to the office due to severe headaches that are increasing in frequency.  The patient describes episodic, right-sided, throbbing or pulsating headaches accompanied by nausea and photophobia.  The headaches began when he was in high school, but lately they have become more frequent and are affecting his work.  The patient takes nonsteroidal analgesics and sumatriptan for the pain and metoclopramide for nausea.  He has no other medical conditions and no drug allergies.  Vital signs are within normal limits, and physical examination shows no abnormalities.  A recent brain imaging study was normal.  Which of the following pharmacotherapies would be most helpful to prevent recurrences of this patient's headache?​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌
explanation:
Migraine therapy

Abortive

  • Triptans
  • NSAIDs, acetaminophen
  • Antiemetics
  • Ergotamine

Preventive

  • Anticonvulsants (topiramate or valproate)
  • Beta blockers
  • Antidepressants (tricyclic or venlafaxine)

NSAIDs = nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

This patient has migraine, a disorder characterized by recurrent, severe, unilateral headaches that are frequently associated with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.  Migraine pharmacotherapies are classified as abortive (to relieve acute pain) or preventive (to reduce the frequency and severity of headaches).  Commonly used abortive medications include mild analgesics (eg, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, acetaminophen), triptans (eg, sumatriptan), antiemetics (eg, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine), and ergotamines.  These medications reduce symptoms at headache onset but do not prevent recurrent headaches.

Patients who have frequent migraines (eg, several in a month) or significant impairment due to the symptoms should receive preventive therapy.  Anticonvulsants such as topiramate can reduce the frequency of migraines, perhaps by decreasing cortical hyperexcitability.  Other preventive medications include beta blockers (eg, metoprolol, propranolol) to regulate vascular pressure changes; tricyclic antidepressants (eg, amitriptyline), which may decrease neuropathic pain; and anti–calcitonin gene–related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibodies (eg, erenumab), which block binding of CGRP to nociceptors.

(Choice A)  Capsaicin is derived from chili peppers and is useful as a topical therapy for neuropathic or musculoskeletal pain.  It is not useful for the treatment of migraine.

(Choice B)  Ergotamine is an agonist at serotonin receptors (5-HT1B/1D/1F) and acts as a vasoconstrictor.  It is used as a migraine abortive treatment, not for prevention.

(Choice C)  Hydrochlorothiazide is an antihypertensive that reduces sodium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule.  Although beta blockers (another type of antihypertensive) are useful for migraine prevention, hydrochlorothiazide is not indicated for treatment of migraine.

(Choice D)  Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) used for depression and anxiety.  Although tricyclic antidepressants and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (eg, venlafaxine) are used for migraine prevention, SSRIs have not been shown to prevent migraines.

Educational objective:Migraine is an episodic disorder characterized by severe, often unilateral headache commonly associated with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.  Treatment is divided into abortive therapy (eg, mild analgesics, triptans, antiemetics, ergotamine) for acute symptoms and preventive therapy (eg, beta blockers, tricyclic antidepressants, anticonvulsants, CGRP monoclonal antibodies) to reduce the frequency of headaches.​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌
